segments: ...and them.
Chronography of Barhebraeus.
...they turned {OCR?} against the envoy of the Mongols and against the Turkmen; and they took their households and whatever they were able to carry,
and fled to Syria,
a complete myriad [ten thousand] of fighting men.
These things happened on Tuesday,
the 29th
(the 19th) of First Kanun in the year 1607
of the Greeks [1607 AG / December 1295 AD].
Now in this year, no one of the tyrannical raiders of Syria went out to this eastern region,
because the blood of the oppressed
and the cry of the poor were heard before God,
and Justice was stirred up against them,
which observes times;
and it visited disasters upon them by means of famine and pestilence that occurred in their lands,
especially in Egypt.
For they say
that Alexandria was completely emptied of inhabitants.
And because this report was not accurately transmitted to us,
we have not enlarged the account upon sweeping rumors {OCR?} from the peoples.
Only that their souls were distressed by famine and pestilence among them,
there is no doubt.
Indeed, how and where and when and at what time,
has not been verified to us up to today.
In the year one thousand and six hundred and eight [1608 AG / 1297 AD] of the Greeks, on the twentieth day of the month of Haziran,
on Monday morning, Ala al-Din conquered the city of Amid,
he who is called the son of Jaja [Ibn Jaja],
having with him a strong force of Arabs who were gathered from the regions of Syria.
And Amid went into bitter captivity;
they took into captivity up to twelve thousand souls,
and many believers were killed,
and even Mor Gregorios, the bishop of that city,
after they made him suffer beatings,
and then they killed him.
And they grew insolent and plundered the great church of the Mother of God,
and burned it with fire.
And its buildings were ruined,
and its arches and its fair and wondrous pillars were thrown down,
and it became a heap of stones from the violence of the burning and the abundance of the flame;
and the fire remained in it for about a month.
And these things happened because the people of Amid rebelled against the lord of Mardin, Malik al-Salih,
and he sent to this man whom we mentioned above in Syria, to come;
and he came and brought with him about twelve thousand [men].
